To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a statistical model predictive for boys needing MCUG or cystoscopy in tertiary care centres is not available.
the anamnesis, uroflowmetry, and ultrasound findings in boys presenting to a tertiary care centre with voiding disorders are not predictive for the presence of urethral obstructing pathology.
a statistical model predictive of urethral obstructing pathology in boys presenting with voided disorders is not possible to construct.

the question, whether a statistical model can be constructed to exclude boys needing cystoscopy.
the question of whether it is possible to construct a predictive statistical model for the presence of urethral obstructed pathology in boys.

we don't know how to predict obstructive pathology in boys.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the anamnesis, the voiding chart and uroflowmetry are not able to predict boys needing further examinations.
we are unable to construct a model to predict urethral obstructing pathology in boys presenting with obstructing voiding symptoms.
the diagnostic workup of boys with voiding dysfunction should be based upon clinical judgment and not on a statistical model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the diagnostic work-up of a boy with voiding disorders should include a cystoscopy, as the statistical model was unable to predict which boys needed it.
we need more knowledge about the pathogenesis of urethral pathology and how to prevent it.
we need to be more humble when trying to predict pathology by a statistical model.
